title: Adverbial participles in a test: kitéve, beismerve

sections.title: What you know
sections.content: You know the adverbial participle in *-va/-ve* from B1 Unit 29: it gives the way or the means of the main action. In texts about science it often keeps an object: *a tévedést beismerve* ('admitting the mistake').

sections.title: What is new
sections.content: This lesson adds the words of testing (*cáfolat*, *cáfolhatóság*, *fallibilizmus*, *demarkációs vonal*) and two fixed participles: *az elméletet cáfolatnak kitéve* ('subjecting the theory to refutation') and *a tévedést beismerve*. Popper's rule: a theory counts as scientific if an observation could in principle refute it.

sections.title: Patterns in Context
rows: A kutatók az elméletet kísérleti cáfolatnak kitéve keresik a hibákat.
Subjecting the theory to experimental refutation, the researchers look for mistakes.
A tévedést beismerve a tudós megőrzi a hitelét.
By admitting the mistake, the scientist keeps his credibility.
A cáfolhatatlan állításokat elutasítva a tudomány elválik a dogmától.
Rejecting claims that cannot be refuted, science separates itself from dogma.
